props.name: renderPointActions
props.description: React actions (e.g. compact edit / delete icon buttons) shown in the card of the active point (hovered, focused or selected), beside its name

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the card of the active point, in place of its name and quadrant (the engine tooltip is not shown)

props.name: quadrantContent
props.description: React content placed over each quadrant (e.g. an add button); the content receives pointer events, the rest of the quadrant does not

props.name: renderQuadrantHeader
props.typeText: ((corner: keyof QuadrantRegions, info: QuadrantHeaderInfo) => ReactNode) | undefined
props.description: React header of each quadrant, in its outer corner (top edge for the top quadrants, bottom edge for the bottom ones, aligned to the outer side); replaces the drawn title, badge, description and count. The header receives pointer events (e.g. an add button)

props.name: accessiblePoints
props.description: Visually hidden list of buttons per quadrant so keyboard and screen reader users can reach the dots: Enter / Space calls `onPointClick`, Shift + arrow keys move the point to the next quadrant (`onPointDrop` with the center of that quadrant); the focused dot gets a focus ring

props.name: getPointProps
props.typeText: ((point: QuadrantPoint, index: number) => Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>) | undefined
props.description: Extra attributes of the invisible anchor placed on each dot (e.g. `data-testid`); every anchor already has `data-point-index` and `data-label` and the class `minerva-chart-quadrant-point`

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip; `false` disables it

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: annotations
props.description: Background areas and reference lines

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

props.name: points
props.description: Points to place

props.name: xDomain
props.description: Range of the horizontal axis

props.name: yDomain
props.description: Range of the vertical axis

props.name: xSplit

props.name: ySplit
props.description: Y value of the horizontal divider (the middle of `yDomain` by default)

props.name: quadrants

props.name: yLabel

props.name: axisLabels

props.name: draggable

events.name: onZoom

events.name: onRendererChange
events.description: Called with the backend once it is ready (and when it falls back after a GPU loss)

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Effort / impact matrix: dots take the color of their quadrant.

examples.title: BCG matrix
examples.description: Product portfolio by relative market share and market growth: xDomain, yDomain, xSplit and ySplit place the dividing lines at a share of 1 and a growth of 10%, reverseX puts the leaders on the left and the dot size is the revenue.

examples.title: Competitor map
examples.description: Pick the two dimensions to compare: the points, xLabel and yLabel follow the selects. Our product has its own color and size, and onPointClick shows a vendor's full profile against ours.

examples.title: Draggable task matrix
examples.description: showTicks={false} and axisLabels turn the chart into a task board: while dragging, the status line names the target quadrant (onPointDrag), and the drop updates the position (onPointDrop); double-click a task to rename it or move it to another quadrant (onPointDoubleClick); click an empty area or the + button (quadrantContent) to add one; renderTooltip fills the card of a task.

examples.title: Eisenhower matrix
examples.description: reverseX puts urgent tasks on the left; onPointClick receives the clicked task.

examples.title: Live service health
examples.description: Latency against error rate for each service, updated every second; the xSplit and ySplit lines are the SLO limits. The services in the critical quadrant are listed with quadrantOf, and renderTooltip formats the units with Intl.

examples.title: Positioning map
examples.description: Price against perceived quality from a customer survey: axisLabels replace the ticks and our brand stands out with its own color and size.

examples.title: Custom quadrant headers
examples.description: renderQuadrantHeader replaces the drawn titles with React content in the outer corner of each quadrant: a badge, the title, an action hint, the count and total time from the info argument, and a + button that adds a task. getPointProps puts a data-testid on the invisible anchor of every dot for end-to-end tests.

examples.title: RICE prioritization
examples.description: Backlog items by effort and by reach × impact, with the dot size following the RICE score; xDomain, yDomain, xSplit and ySplit set the scales and thresholds. The switch weights the value by confidence, which drops the speculative bets, and renderTooltip lists the four RICE inputs.

examples.title: Risk matrix
examples.description: Project risks scored from 1 to 5 by likelihood and impact, with quadrant colors from accept (green) to act now (red); click a risk to select it, an empty area to clear.

examples.title: SWOT analysis
examples.description: showTicks={false} and axisLabels turn the chart into a SWOT grid. quadrantContent adds a count badge in the inner corner of each quadrant, onQuadrantClick lists its factors and fades the others, and onPointClick names the clicked factor.

examples.title: Talent calibration
examples.description: Performance against potential during a calibration session. onPointDrag reads out the scores and the target quadrant while dragging, onPointDrop saves the move, and onPointDoubleClick puts a person back where they started; moved people get a bigger dot.

examples.title: Badges, counts and keyboard moves
examples.description: Quadrants show badges, descriptions and counts. Hovering or focusing a task shows a detached translucent card beside its point, with its name, quadrant and actions. The point keeps its real size and position; the card stays clear of it and changes sides when space is limited. The card replaces its label; the card goes when the pointer leaves, with Escape or with a click beside the tasks. A selected task keeps a ring. While a task is dragged the card follows it and names the quadrant it would land in. Tab enters the task list, Enter selects, and Shift + arrows move tasks between quadrants with live announcements.

QuadrantChartProps.onPointClick: Called with the clicked point and its index
QuadrantChartProps.onPointDoubleClick: Called with the point and its index when the same dot is clicked twice quickly
QuadrantChartProps.onPointDrag: Called with the point, its index and the quadrant under the pointer on every move of a dragged dot, before the drop (the dot does not move until onPointDrop)
QuadrantChartProps.onQuadrantClick: Called with the quadrant and the data position when the empty area of a quadrant is clicked
QuadrantChartProps.onPointDrop: Called with the point, its index and the drop target when a dragged dot is released; setting it makes the dots draggable (update points to move them)
QuadrantChartProps.renderPointActions: React actions (e.g. compact edit / delete icon buttons) shown in the card of the active point, beside its name: the hovered or focused point, else the selected one (with actions, the selected point keeps its card); receives the point and its index
QuadrantChartProps.renderTooltip: React content of the card of the active point, in place of its name and quadrant (the engine tooltip is not shown)
QuadrantChartProps.quadrantContent: React content placed over each quadrant (e.g. an add button); only that content receives pointer events
QuadrantChartProps.renderQuadrantHeader: React header of each quadrant in its outer corner (top edge for the top quadrants, bottom edge for the bottom ones); receives the corner and { count, points, indices, region } and replaces the drawn title, badge, description and count
QuadrantChartProps.accessiblePoints: Visually hidden list of buttons per quadrant for keyboard and screen reader users: arrow keys move between the points, Enter / Space calls onPointClick, Shift + arrow keys move the point to the next quadrant (onPointDrop, announced in a live region), and the focused dot gets a focus ring and is reported by onHover. Vue, Angular and Web Components (no-accessible-points) render the same layer; React Native exposes each point with ‘Move to …’ accessibility actions, and Taro, uni-app and WeChat a list of the points with ‘Move to …’ buttons
QuadrantChartProps.getPointProps: Extra attributes (e.g. data-testid) of the invisible anchor placed on each dot; every anchor has data-point-index, data-label and the class minerva-chart-quadrant-point

QuadrantConfig.selectedIndices: Indices of the selected points, each drawn with a ring

props.hideTicks: Hides the numeric ticks of the axes (only the matrix remains)
props.hideLabels: Hides the labels next to the dots
props.dragPoints: Lets the user drag the dots (minerva-point-drag while moving, minerva-point-drop on release; update points to move them); also enables the Shift + arrow moves of the keyboard
props.noAccessiblePoints: Leaves out the visually hidden list of the dots (arrows between the dots, Enter to click, Shift + arrows to move the focused dot, focus ring)
props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.activeIndex: Index of the point whose card shows the point-actions slot: the hovered point, else the keyboard-focused one, else selectedIndex (null: none, or during a drag); read only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-point-click: A dot was clicked; detail: { point, index }
events.minerva-point-double-click: The same dot was clicked twice in quick succession; detail: { point, index }
events.minerva-quadrant-click: The empty area of a quadrant was clicked; detail: { quadrant, x, y }
events.minerva-point-drag: A dot is being dragged (on every move, before the drop); detail: { point, index, x, y, quadrant }
events.minerva-point-drop: A dragged dot was released, or the focused dot was moved with Shift + an arrow key; detail: { point, index, x, y, quadrant }
events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

slots.quadrant-header-top-left: Header of the top-left quadrant, in its outer corner (replaces its drawn title, badge, description and count)
slots.point-actions: Actions shown in the point card of the active point, beside its name (e.g. compact edit / delete buttons); with actions, the selected point keeps its card; it receives pointer events

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
